title: The U.S. Is Pushing for Ukraine Peace Talks. Is Putin Interested?
gist: David Ignatius argues the US-European-Ukrainian Oslo peace framework is real but one-sided until Putin responds to Steve Witkoff's St. Petersburg briefing. Trump's diesel-purchase deal and Russia sanctions waiver, triggered by Zelensky's refusal to stop refinery strikes, disrupted the effort.

insights.claim: US and European envoys have worked with Ukraine on an agenda for talks with Russia covering mutual security guarantees, postwar economic integration and reconstruction, and territorial compromises.
insights.speaker: David Ignatius
insights.so_what: Defines the scope of any settlement; watch for territorial and security-guarantee terms that would shape reconstruction flows.

insights.claim: The Ukraine peace track has Ukrainian and European support but no Russian buy-in; the Kremlin has not even agreed to talk about talks.
insights.speaker: David Ignatius
insights.so_what: Default expectation should be no near-term ceasefire until Moscow signals acceptance.
insights.quote: A real peace pact would be a symphony. But we have the sound of one hand clapping.

insights.claim: If Putin accepts, the sequence is trilateral Russia-Ukraine-US talks on a ceasefire line, monitoring and occupied territories, then multilateral talks with Europe on reconstruction and Russia-Europe energy relations.
insights.speaker: David Ignatius
insights.so_what: A positive sequence would reopen the question of European energy ties with Russia, relevant to gas and power markets.
insights.locator: If Putin agrees to Witkoff's request

insights.claim: Ignatius warns Putin may be luring the US down a negotiating path with hints of concessions he will not make, as Israeli and Palestinian leaders did for decades with US peace processors.
insights.speaker: David Ignatius
insights.so_what: Treat Russian signals of flexibility skeptically; do not price in a settlement on rhetoric.

insights.claim: A Putin rejection would at least show who blocked the peace effort and might convince Trump to stop making concessions to Russia.
insights.speaker: David Ignatius
insights.so_what: A Putin refusal could be a catalyst for firmer US policy and sanctions enforcement.

insights.claim: Trump's anger began when Zelensky rejected requests since late summer to halt drone attacks on Russian refineries to lower US fuel prices ahead of the midterms; Trump then struck a diesel deal and waived a Russia sanctions law he had just signed.
insights.speaker: David Ignatius
insights.so_what: US fuel-price politics is directly shaping sanctions policy; refinery strikes and sanctions waivers move diesel and crude differentials.
insights.locator: What seems to have lit Trump's fuse

insights.claim: Zelensky said he had asked for Starlink access for deep strikes into Russia, which would limit attacks to precision strikes on ballistic missile and drone production facilities, according to Ron Wahid of Magellan Investments.
insights.speaker: David Ignatius
insights.so_what: Shows Ukraine's refinery campaign is a choice about targeting, with energy-market consequences if constrained.

insights.claim: Amid the quarrel, reports said the US halted early-warning intelligence on Russian ballistic missile attacks and curbed Starlink guidance for Ukrainian drones; a US official said intelligence was again flowing freely.
insights.speaker: David Ignatius
insights.so_what: US leverage over Ukraine's defense via intelligence and Starlink is a live pressure point.

insights.claim: Russia released American teacher Stephen Hubbard before the Witkoff visit, a goodwill gesture to Trump that Ignatius says does nothing to advance peace.
insights.speaker: David Ignatius
insights.so_what: Symbolic Russian gestures to Trump should not be read as substantive concessions.
insights.locator: The St. Petersburg meeting was sweetened

insights.claim: Finland's Stubb called Oslo 'genuine progress' and Zelensky cited a US-European offer of NATO-like security guarantees and sensitive issues including territory.
insights.speaker: David Ignatius
insights.so_what: NATO-like guarantees for Ukraine are on the table; the territory question remains unresolved.
insights.locator: Zelensky was on his best behavior
